id: title:jonmcwest:let people resize the trace dialog inspector

review.posthog_relevance: Frontend user experience and workflow efficiency in the TraceDialog component, specifically preserving user-selected inspector width across page reloads and dialog re-opens.
review.reason: The change replaces a fixed, media-query-dependent layout with a dynamic, user-controlled inspector width using a Resizer component and CSS variables. P1.F1.H2 adds persistent state management, while P1.F1.H3 removes the media-query constraints and applies the dynamic width. review.uncertainty: The benefit relies on the implementation of the Resizer component and CSS variable usage, which are observed. The actual user benefit depends on the correctness of the resizer implementation and the compatibility of the CSS variables, which are not independently verified. No production incident or adoption data is available.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No score assigned; tier requires assessment.

observations.behavior: Adds a Resizer component and its associated state management to the TraceDialog, replacing a fixed-width, media-query-dependent layout with a dynamic, user-controlled inspector width.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows the TraceDialog's inspector pane to retain and restore a user-selected width, rather than resetting to a default or media-query-based width on every open. This preserves the user's preferred inspection view state across page reloads or dialog re-opens, supporting the PostHog workflow of inspecting traces without repeatedly re-sizing the inspector.
